_comment: Findings-report corpora. The report generator knows nothing about any
particular comparison; a corpus profile tells it which repos the findings
cite, where the captured evidence lives, and how to turn a path as written
in a finding into a path inside a repo. Adding a corpus is a data edit,
not a script change.
A run picks its corpus from, in order: an explicit --corpus flag, the
backlog's top-level "corpus" field, .corpus-meta.json, then the default
below. See tim/src/parity/corpus-profile.js, which copies the precedence
of tools/journey-builder/target-profile.sh.
sides[] is a list, not a pair. The requirements side will not always be a
prototype and there will not always be two of them; nothing here assumes
the number two. repos{} is keyed by repo, not by side, because a finding
on the frontend side routinely cites the backend.
pathRoots is ordered longest-first and each entry strips its prefix to
leave a repo-relative path. The bare prefixes come last because they are
prefixes of nothing else; impliedPrefix re-normalises a path that was
already repo-relative when it was written.
A side does not name where its capture specs live. That is computed from
workarea by tim/src/parity/capture/run.js, and a second copy here would be
a second source of truth that nothing reads.
This file lives in tools/ rather than tim/src/ because the shell entry
points in this directory read it too.

dr1.description: The live-animals frontend against Design release 1 — the signed-off visual definition of the service, served at the prototype's root URLs. A work list, not a negotiation: where the frontend differs from DR1 the frontend is wrong.
_bandComment: How a comparison sorts its findings is a property of that comparison,
so the taxonomy is data here rather than a constant in the renderer.
The DR2.1 bands were written for a negotiation over a design still in
flux, where a finding had to earn its place before anyone would build
it. DR1 is signed off, so a finding is born as accepted work and the
only question left is whether the finding itself is right.
Order is render order: the report shows these sections top to bottom.
A corpus that declares no bands falls back to the historic three. See

sides.label: Frontend
sides._sourcePathComment: The capture directory is named after the last commit that touched src, not HEAD, so editing the harness does not orphan identical pixels.
_appComment: STUB_MODE is what makes the frontend self-contained. Without it the
service wants the real Defra ID round-trip and the real backend,
address book and reference data, none of which a capture run starts;
the first request is then bounced to an identity provider that is not
there. The frontend's own playwright.config.js sets the same flag on
its webServer for the same reason. `npm run fit:start` does not build
the client bundle, so .public must already hold one — a capture of an
unstyled page is worse than no capture.
3005, not 3000. The workspace stack runs its own build of this
frontend on 3000, and tim uses whatever is already listening rather
than starting a second copy — so with the stack up, a capture on
3000 photographs the container instead of the stubbed run these
specs are written against, and says nothing about having done so.
A port the stack does not own removes the ambiguity rather than
relying on nobody having the stack up.

sides.label: Design release 1
_appComment: DR1 IS the root URLs. app/views/index.html is a release chooser
and calls the root journey 'the current design release journey at
the root URLs'; app/routes.js mounts only testing,
design-release-2 and design-release-2.1, so the root router is DR1.
3010: the workspace stack already owns 3000/3001/3007/3100/3200.
Serve the kit in dev mode (`npm run dev`), not `serve`: production
mode forces https on a plaintext server and sets secure-only
cookies, which breaks the kit's sessions over http. The kit accepts
TCP connections before an HTTP probe settles under Node 24, so wait
on the port rather than on a request.

_captureComment: What the pictures on disk are actually of. A pin is where the
citations point; a capture is where the pixels came from. Capture ids
are immutable — a capture at a new commit writes a new directory
rather than overwriting the old one — so this is the one place that
says which directory the comparison rests on.

frontend.note: Complete. All 33 screens the enumerator names plus 7 states of them, across 19 tests in 6 specs, each with a full-page shot, a page model and the rendered DOM. The sha is the last commit that touched src, not HEAD: naming the directory after HEAD orphaned every picture each time the capture harness itself was edited, and those pixels were identical. The states exist because findings needed them, and one of them is the only picture of an actual defect in the corpus: fe-hub-exit-details-blocked shows the Exit details row present, unlinked, and reading 'Cannot start yet' under a reason for which port of exit was already answered.

prototype.note: Complete. 42 screens across six specs — all 23 pages DR1 has, plus 19 states of them. Coverage reports nothing missing and nothing unexplained. The last two states were added once findings needed them: dr1-roles-and-addresses-partial is the only state in which DR1 renders its Same-as address shortcuts, and dr1-review-notification-incomplete the only one showing the per-card error state a user meets when they open review early.

which detail became final — for this corpus that is the first ingest,
which composed detail from the authored slots and froze it. After it, a
citation may never be deleted and detail may never change at all.

dr1b.description: An independent second reading of the same live-animals frontend against the same signed-off Design release 1, over the identical captured evidence. Written to be compared against EUDPA-328-DR1 rather than to replace it: the pictures are the same, so every difference between the two backlogs is a difference of judgement.
_verificationComment: Refuse a first ingest of any finding no verifier recorded looking at.
A correction leaves a trace when it fires and the non-firing case
leaves none, so without the record nothing distinguishes a verifier
that found nothing from one that looked at nothing — and ingest
freezes detail permanently, so the record has to exist first.

_enumeratorComment: Deliberately dr1s, not a copy. Which screens each application HAS is a
fact about the applications, not a judgement about them, and this run is
an independent second reading of the JUDGEMENT over identical evidence.
Re-deriving the enumeration would change what the two runs are being
compared on. It also means this run does not exercise SCREEN_ENUMERATOR,
which is stated rather than quietly true.
_captureComment: Byte-for-byte copies of dr1s captures, at the same two shas, so both
runs read the same pixels, the same page models and the same rendered
DOM. Copied rather than shared: anchors --write and a re-capture both
write into evidenceRoot, and a second corpus pointing at dr1s would
overwrite the evidence 133 ruled-on findings rest on.
_baselineComment: The commit at which detail became final for this corpus: the first ingest, which composed detail from the authored slots and froze it. After it, a citation may never be deleted and detail may never change at all.
I1 to I3 compare the backlog against the git blob at this ref rather than a copy on disk, so the oracle cannot drift.
